newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Independent Belgrade radio shut down.
newsitem.headline: Independent Belgrade radio shut down.

text.p: Serbian authorities shut down Belgrade's only independent radio station B-92 on Tuesday amid a wave of opposition street protests against President Slobodan Milosevic, radio staff said.
The transmitter used by Radio B-92, which unlike state broadcasters had given wide coverage to the anti-government demonstrations, was switched off, editor-in-chief Veran Matic said.
The station received a letter from the federal ministry of transport and communication saying the radio was operating illegally, he said

"This means our radio is practically shut down," Matic told Reuters. "This is obviously only the finish of what has been happening in the past ten days, the stifling of B-92, an attempt to fully solve the 'problem' of radio B-92."
The radio's signal was jammed for several days and went off the air as of 3 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Tuesday.
Unlike state television and radio, Radio B-92 has covered street demonstrations that have shaken the capital Belgrade and other towns for more than two weeks.

The radio, one of a handful of independent radio stations in Serbia, complained its signal was being jammed over the past several days and began sending news over the Internet in Serbo-Croat and English.
The crackdown came despite appeals from Western powers to protect independent media and underlined Milosevic's government was taking an increasingly tough line to halt street demonstrations.
Accusations that ruling socialists committed massive poll fraud in local elections this month set off the protests which have caused Milosevic political damage at home and abroad.
Milosevic last shut down Radio B-92 in 1991, when similar street demonstrations hit the capital. Police occupied the radio studio but B-92 resumed broadcasting within 24 hours.

Radio B-92 started operating on May 15, 1989 and its contract with state Radio Television Serbia expired in 1990. Since then the radio applied for a frequency but was never awarded a broadcasting license.
The letter from federal authorities said: "On examining our evidence we determined that your radio station B-92 does not have the authorisation for work issued in your name B-92.
"The work of your radio station without authorisation is illegal."
